exposure: maternal stress coping styles (cognitive restructuring, problem avoidance, problem solving)
severity of neonatal health problems (Clinical Risk Index for Babies - CRIB score)
cohort: The study included 401 mothers, comprising 125 whose infants were admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and 276 mothers whose infants did not require NICU care.
finding: While no differences were found in PPD or bonding between NICU and non-NICU groups, cognitive restructuring, problem avoidance, severity of neonatal health problems during the first 12 hours of life, and problem solving were identified as predictors of postpartum depression in the NICU group.
cross-section timing: Data on PPD, bonding, and coping strategies were collected six weeks after birth, while newborn illness severity was assessed throughout NICU admission and within the first 12 hours of life.
